metadata.note: The Mississippi Central Railroad (Pearl and Leaf Rivers Railroad renamed 13 Feb 1904; consolidated with the Natchez and Eastern 15 Jun 1909): the 149-mile Hattiesburg - Prentiss - Brookhaven - Natchez road in south Mississippi. Passenger trains 1904 (earliest confirmed) to 27/28 Feb 1941; freight only thereafter; sold to the Illinois Central 29 Mar 1967, 26 years after passengers ended, so there is no Rule 4 split. Drawn as three features because the three sections opened to passengers in different years (1904, 1906, 1908). NOT the 1850s Mississippi Central (Canton - Grenada - Jackson, Tenn.), which the IC absorbed in 1877 and which is drawn inside illinois_central.geojson; Wikipedia's 'Mississippi Central Railroad' article and its '1941' are about that road.
sources: research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt (Feb 1952 Official Guide, MC table 'Freight Service only')

0.36 mi of ex-G&SI track (old_railway_operator=IC) at Hattiesburg; 4.4 mi of untagged CN Central Subdivision track east of Brookhaven.
metadata.color_note: #2F6B4F is new: checked programmatically that no other company in data/ uses it. Deliberately not the IC's #F4801F.
omitted_blocks: [4] Camp Shelby branch (WWI) - drawable NONE: the only passenger marker is Fowler's own 'pass?'.
[5] Pascagoula Extension, Hattiesburg - Pines - logging extension, no passenger evidence.
[6] leased GM&N Hattiesburg - Beaumont (1921-c.1924) - no confirmed passenger year (Motorcar 300 is only a hint).
[7] leased Tallahala Branch - logging line, no passenger evidence.
[8] Pearl and Leaf Rivers pre-1904 - no dated passenger year; if one is found, extend mc-hattiesburg-atwood back rather than adding a feature.
not_yet_sourced: mc-hattiesburg-atwood starts [OPEN] at 1904, the earliest CONFIRMED year (1904 Official Guide via Fowler); P&LR passenger service c.1898-1903 is possible but undated. A pre-1904 Official Guide or an ICC 'operation began' date would settle it.
mc-atwood-brookhaven starts at 1906; Prentiss - Silver Creek (built 1904) may have carried passengers 1904-1905.

The Feb 1941 end rests on secondary sources (Garraway blog, MRH forum, USM finding-aid summary) that may share a source; a Feb-Mar 1941 Hattiesburg American / Natchez Democrat story or a Mississippi Railroad Commission order would confirm it.
Frequency before the mid-1930s; headway 720 and avg_speed 36 km/h are estimates from Garraway's memory.
Camp Shelby WWI passenger service (1918-1919 likely) and MC motor-car service on the leased GM&N Hattiesburg - Beaumont (1921-c.1924) - candidates if sourced.
P&LR charter date conflict: ICC 27 Nov 1897 vs msrailroads.com 20 Nov 1897 (does not affect the map).

properties.speed_source: estimated: Garraway's remembered mid-1930s times for westbound No. 1, Bassfield 7:34 -> Natchez 12:45 (116 mi in 5h11m), give about 22 mph / 36 km/h including stops. A memory, not a published timetable (Rule 3).
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap ways tagged old_railway_operator=Mississippi Central - almost entirely the Longleaf Trace rail-trail (highway=cycleway, railway=abandoned), which follows the MC roadbed lifted in the early 1990s - plus 0.36 mi of the ex-G&SI (CN Beaumont Subdivision, old_railway_operator=IC, way 341238447) into Hattiesburg. Traced with opstrace.py; Douglas-Peucker 8 m, then trim_reversals. Waypoints: Nominatim town centres (Hattiesburg, Sumrall, Bassfield, Carson), Prentiss hand-pinned (Nominatim returned Prentiss COUNTY in north Mississippi).
properties.geometry_quality: Drawn 42.2 mi against a documented 43 mi (Fowler mileposts Hattiesburg 0.0 -> Atwood 43). 41.8 mi on ways tagged old_railway_operator=Mississippi Central (41.7 mi of it the Longleaf Trace rail-trail), 0.36 mi on the G&SI; NO straight-line or approximated leg. Hattiesburg end: the trace leaves the MC grade where it meets the G&SI and runs 0.36 mi south on G&SI track to about the Hattiesburg depot, matching the ICC's 0.41 mi of MC trackage rights over the G&SI there; the exact 1904-1910 passenger terminal was not located. Atwood end is NOT a geocode: Nominatim returned 'Polk-Atwood Road', ~8 km north of the line, so Atwood is placed on the traced line 1.2 mi east of Prentiss (Fowler: Atwood 43, Prentiss 44.2), Prentiss itself being a hand-pinned town centre the line passes 0.1 km from - Atwood is good to perhaps +/-0.5 mi. Milepost check (trace vs Fowler): Sumrall 17.8 vs 18.7, Bassfield 31.8 vs 32.9, Carson 36.7 vs 37.5, Prentiss 43.4 vs 44.2 - a steady ~1 mi short, consistent with Fowler's 0.0 lying slightly east of where the drawn line starts. Alignment era: drawn on the line as OSM records it at its last state (the 1990s-lifted grade / Longleaf Trace and today's CN / Natchez Railway track); the report records no main-line relocation 1904-1941, but none was checked for either.

segments.note: Mississippi Central main line, east end: Hattiesburg - Breland - Epley - Sumrall - Melba (Lott) - Bassfield - Carson - Atwood (Fowler mileposts 0 -> 43). The Pearl and Leaf Rivers Railroad (J.J. Newman Lumber Co. road west from Hattiesburg) was renamed Mississippi Central on 13 Feb 1904 - the same company, not a Rule 4 split. START IS [OPEN]: 1904 is the EARLIEST CONFIRMED passenger year (Fowler cites the 1904 Official Guide for Lott and Atwood), NOT a known start. Passengers may have ridden the P&LR earlier (Hattiesburg - Sumrall, c.1898-1903; an undated photo of a P&LR passenger train at Epley exists), but no source dates it. Do not extend back without evidence. From 1906 trains ran on to Brookhaven and from 1908 through to Natchez (see the other two features). headway_min 720 is an ESTIMATE: two round trips a day (Nos. 1/3 westbound, 2/4 eastbound) in the mid-1930s, from Garraway's memory, not a timetable; frequency before the mid-1930s is NOT SOURCED and is carried back unverified. Passenger service ended with the last eastbound train on 27 Feb 1941 and the last westbound on 28 Feb 1941 (Garraway eyewitness blog; Latham, MRH forum locomotive histories; USM 'Railroad Collection' finding aid, seen only as a search summary), consistent with the Feb 1952 Official Guide printing the MC as 'Freight Service only'. These secondary sources may not be independent. Buses (Tri-State Transit, later Trailways) replaced the trains. Freight continued: Mississippi Central to 1967, then Illinois Central / ICG / CN - not drawn (Rule 1).

segments.note: Mississippi Central main line, middle: Atwood - Prentiss - Whitesand - Silver Creek - Wanilla (Smith's Ferry) - Sontag - Woolworth - Heucks - Brookhaven (Fowler mileposts 43 -> 83.3). Prentiss - Silver Creek was built in 1904 and Silver Creek - Brookhaven in 1905-1906 (ICC valuation); passengers on Prentiss - Silver Creek in 1904-1905 are likely but unconfirmed, as no station east of Atwood carries a 1904G or 1905G mark. 1906 is the first confirmed year (Fowler's 1906 Official Guide marks: Smith's Ferry, Farmer, Rafn, Heucks Retreat, Friendship). Connections: G&SI Columbia branch at Silver Creek, GM&O at Wanilla, IC main line at Brookhaven. Garraway's mid-1930s westbound No. 1: Prentiss 8:00, Silver Creek 8:26, Wanilla 8:50, Brookhaven 9:51. headway_min 720 is an ESTIMATE: two round trips a day (Nos. 1/3 westbound, 2/4 eastbound) in the mid-1930s, from Garraway's memory, not a timetable; frequency before the mid-1930s is NOT SOURCED and is carried back unverified. segments.note: Mississippi Central main line, west end: Brookhaven - Zetus - Lucien - McCall - Eddiceton - Bude - Meadville - Roxie - Cranfield - Washington - St. Catherine - Natchez (Fowler mileposts 83.3 -> 149.0). Built in 1908 by the Natchez and Eastern Railway, consolidated into the Mississippi Central on 15 Jun 1909; no evidence the N&E ran trains under its own name, and the 1908 first through passenger train is described as a Mississippi Central train from Hattiesburg - so no Rule 4 split. Start 1908: msrailroads.com, 'In 1908 the much publicized first through passenger train was pulled from Hattiesburg to Natchez'; Fowler shows St. Catherines in the 1909 Guide. Connections: Y&MV (IC) at Roxie; Natchez & Southern, Louisiana Midland and IC at Natchez.
